findings.body: yoh set out to delete the contents-API write path, but cloudflare/src/git-contents.ts survives as repo-room.ts's publish mechanism (create/update against one ref over the contents API). That keeps alive the defect class yoh named (99f: the ref goes in the query on a read and in the body on a write) on the one path still using it. Either move the publish into the container's git or record why the room must keep the API.
findings.title: Decide whether the repo room's publish still needs the GitHub contents API now the orchestrator has a clone

findings.body: u9h (dha's live gate run) still says to run an epic 'through EpicReconcilerWorkflow', which yoh deleted. It is also now the only place yoh's acceptance (ticfac drives a cloud epic in the container; a killed orchestrator re-derives from the remote) is proven live. Its acceptance should name that run: SIGTERM flush of a startProcess'd orchestrator, adoption after a mid-run restart, waitForEvent timeout concluded from the branch.
findings.title: Restate u9h's gate run for the yoh shape: ticfac run-epic in the container, not EpicReconcilerWorkflow

findings.body: In yoh, the same host-dependent runstate maintenance fixture failure was drafted as a separate finding by nine ticks (all later promoted to pqs), and 9iz re-drafted b1t's wall-bound gap. Each duplicate costs a triage step on a run that is meant to be unattended. Keying findings on the failing test or symbol and suppressing re-drafts of an open one would remove that load.
findings.title: A finding that reproduces at the base is matched against existing findings and ticks before it is drafted
